paragraphs: Yosef HaBavli. (A tanna of a baraita.)

In [Menachot 18a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.18a.4-6): Rabbi said, "When I went —" to Rabbi Elazar ben Shammua, "I found Yosef HaBavli sitting before him, and he was especially dear to him, up to one particular point, he said to him, 'Rabbi,' —" the face of Yosef HaBavli beamed — the eyes of (Rabbi Elazar ben Shammua, abbreviated ראב״ש) shed tears; he said, "Happy are you, Torah scholars, for whom words of Torah are especially dear," and applied to him the verse "How I love Your Torah" — and there it is implied that he also studied with Rabbi Yehuda.

In [Yevamot 74a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.74a.9), Hyman quotes a question about who disagrees with Rabbi Akiva, followed by the name Rabbi Yosef HaBavli and a baraita with his ruling.[^4] And in the Tosefta, Parah chapter 4: "Rabbi Yosef HaBavli says: one lacking atonement is disqualified." And in [Pesachim 113b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.113b.18) and [Yoma 52b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.52b.6): "A tanna — he is Yosef ish Hutzal; he is Yosef HaBavli." And see the entry Isi ben Yehuda.

notes.text: Hyman abbreviates the exchange. Rashi explains עד לאחת as reaching a particular halakhah; Tosafot cites explanations meaning “exceedingly” or “as dear as one’s own life.” The rendering here follows Rashi.

The consulted Menachot 18a has Yosef’s face beaming and Elazar ben Shammua’s eyes shedding tears. Rashi’s particular-halakhah explanation and Tosafot’s exceedingly/life explanations were directly inspected; Hyman’s elisions and inferred Yehudah studentship are retained.

The two lists use different forms for the final name: [Pesachim 113b:18](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.113b.18) has Issi ben Akavya, and [Yoma 52b:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.52b.6) has Issi ben Akiva. Hyman quotes only the opening equivalence in this entry.

The consulted [Yevamot 74a:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.74a.9) describes the dissenting opinion as that of the tanna in the baraita who disagrees with Rabbi Yosef HaBavli. Rabbi Yosef himself rules that burning the red heifer is invalid if done by someone who still lacks atonement.
